outcome: No source I could open records an event after 26 January 2024 that settles, moves, or checks this bullet. The bullet's status rests on pre-window work (Shelah 1983, Lessmann 2003, Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah arXiv August 2023), which covers the question only conditionally (excellence) or only for aleph_1 with a model-size hypothesis. The in-window items I found that touch atomic classes or categoricity concern other questions.
problem_asks: (1) Hypothesis: the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory T is categorical in aleph_n. The statement says 'the aleph_n' with no n fixed and no 'every'. Read literally it is one unspecified n. The sources treat two readings: a single n (the aleph_1 case is the one studied in the literature) or every n (Shelah's hypothesis). (2) Conclusion: the class is categorical in every cardinal, meaning for every cardinal kappa there is exactly one atomic model of T of size kappa up to isomorphism. The literal wording includes aleph_0 and the finite cardinals as well as all uncountable cardinals. (3) Implicit: the statement does not say T is countable, but every source I found assumes a countable T (Shelah's excellence results and Lessmann's theorem are stated for countable T).

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Classification theory for non-elementary classes I: the number of uncountable models of psi in L_{omega1,omega}. Part A', Israel J. Math. 46(3) (1983) 212-240. For atomic models of a countable T the paper isolates 'excellent' classes (an n-amalgamation property for all n and all cardinalities). Its ZFC theorem: an excellent atomic class with an uncountable model has models of arbitrarily large cardinality, and if it is categorical in one uncountable power it is categorical in all uncountable powers. The converse, as stated in the 2023 Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah paper (Section 1): if 2^{aleph_n} < 2^{aleph_{n+1}} for all n, an atomic class with an uncountable model that is categorical in every aleph_n is excellent. I did not check that converse in Shelah's own text. Part B (cited as [She83b]) was not opened.
events.revisions: Dated to the journal year. The first circulated preprint was not located, so no month is given.
events.delivers: Within excellent atomic classes of a countable T: categoricity in one uncountable cardinal implies categoricity in every uncountable cardinal. Excellence is a hypothesis of this theorem, not a consequence of categoricity. Categoricity in every aleph_n yields excellence only under the very weak GCH (2^{aleph_n} < 2^{aleph_{n+1}} for all n), per the 2023 paper's citation of this result. The uncountable transfer says nothing about aleph_0 or finite cardinals.
events.remains: Whether categoricity in a single aleph_n (rather than every aleph_n, and without the very weak GCH) yields excellence in ZFC. That is the case the bullet asks about on its single-n reading. Categoricity at aleph_0 and at finite cardinals is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Israel Journal of Mathematics (refereed journal of record); author Saharon Shelah
checked_by.what_they_did: Published Part A after refereeing. I did not see a referee report or any separate verification.

events.direction: Conditional positive. Under excellence, categoricity in one uncountable cardinal transfers to all uncountable cardinals. This does not by itself settle the bullet, because excellence is not derived from categoricity in a single aleph_n in this result.

events.what_happened: R. Grossberg and B. Hart, 'The classification of excellent classes', J. Symbolic Logic 54(4) (1989) 1359-1381. Concerns excellent classes defined through excellent Scott sentences. Recalls Shelah's result that an excellent Scott sentence categorical in some uncountable power is categorical in all uncountable powers, and notes that the omega-saturated models of an omega-stable theory form an excellent class. A search query gave 1987; the publisher page gives 1989.
events.delivers: Background to the excellence route. Restates the conditional transfer (excellence plus categoricity in one uncountable power gives all uncountable powers) for excellent Scott sentences. Gives no new categoricity result for atomic classes of a first-order theory.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of record); authors R. Grossberg and B. Hart
checked_by.what_they_did: Published. I read only the opening of the extract on the publisher page, not the paper.

events.direction: Background. Restates the conditional direction: excellence plus categoricity in one uncountable power gives categoricity in all uncountable powers.

events.what_happened: B. Hart and S. Shelah, 'Categoricity over P for first order T or categoricity for phi in L_{omega1,omega} can stop at aleph_k while holding for aleph_0, ..., aleph_{k-1}', arXiv math/9201240 (submitted 15 Jan 1990), Israel J. Math. 70 (1990) 219-235. Per the arXiv abstract as my fetch summarised it: for each k > 0 a complete first-order theory T_k and an L_{omega1,omega} sentence phi_k, both categorical (relatively, for T_k) at aleph_n for n < k, but not categorical at beth_k. The title says the failure is at aleph_k; the abstract as summarised says beth_k. Not resolved from the abstract alone.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (15 Jan 1990). Journal: Israel J. Math. 70 (1990) 219-235.
events.delivers: A ZFC family of counterexamples: categoricity at aleph_0 through aleph_{k-1} does not carry over to beth_k for these L_{omega1,omega} sentences. So finitely many aleph_n-categoricities do not, in general, give categoricity further up. The results concern an L_{omega1,omega} sentence and a 'categoricity over P' notion, not the atomic class of a complete first-order theory.
events.remains: Whether an atomic class of a complete first-order T can be built with the same behaviour. The abstract does not say the examples are atomic classes, and the bullet's single-aleph_n case is not decided.

checked_by.who: Israel Journal of Mathematics (refereed journal of record); authors Bradd Hart and Saharon Shelah
checked_by.what_they_did: Published after refereeing. No referee report seen.

events.doubts: Title and abstract disagree on the cardinal (aleph_k in the title, beth_k in the abstract as summarised by the fetch tool). The construction was not read. Resolving this needs the paper text.
events.direction: Cuts against a general transfer from finitely many aleph_n-categoricities, for L_{omega1,omega} sentences. The first-order theories T_k in the abstract are complete, but the sentences that carry the categoricity are L_{omega1,omega}.
events.object: A family indexed by k > 0: a complete first-order theory T_k and an L_{omega1,omega} sentence phi_k, categorical at aleph_0 through aleph_{k-1} and failing categoricity at the next stage (aleph_k per the title, beth_k per the abstract summary). The construction was not read, so whether it is explicit is not established.

events.what_happened: O. Lessmann, 'Categoricity and U-rank in excellent classes', J. Symbolic Logic 68(4) (2003) 1317-1336, DOI 10.2178/jsl/1067620189. Studies the class of atomic models of a countable first-order theory. Per the abstract: if the class is excellent and categorical in some uncountable cardinal, then each model is prime and minimal over the basis of a definable pregeometry given by a quasiminimal set, and so the class is categorical in every uncountable cardinal. Also defines a U-rank for complete types over models. It is finite in the uncountably categorical excellent case, and its supremum may be omega without being attained, unlike the first-order case.
events.revisions: No preprint of this paper was found. The arXiv item math/9704206 (1997) by Lessmann is a different paper, 'Ranks and pregeometries in finite diagrams', and is not used here.
events.delivers: Conditional on excellence: for the atomic class of a countable first-order T, categoricity in some uncountable cardinal gives categoricity in every uncountable cardinal, via the pregeometry structure of the models.
events.remains: Excellence itself. The paper does not show that excellence follows from categoricity in a single aleph_n. Categoricity at aleph_0 and at finite cardinals is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of record); author Olivier Lessmann
checked_by.what_they_did: Published after refereeing. I saw the abstract and metadata only; the full text is paywalled and was not read.

events.direction: Conditional positive, the same direction as Shelah 1983: excellence plus categoricity in one uncountable cardinal gives categoricity in all uncountable cardinals.

events.what_happened: M. Bays, B. Hart, T. Hyttinen, M. Kesala and J. Kirby, 'Quasiminimal structures and excellence', Bull. London Math. Soc. 46(1) (2014) 155-163, DOI 10.1112/blms/bdt076 (online 2013). Shows that the excellence axiom in the definition of Zilber's quasiminimal excellent classes is redundant, since it follows from the other axioms. Says this simplifies categoricity proofs.
events.revisions: Online (2013) and issue (2014) years differ. The first public date was not pinned down beyond the year.
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet. The setting is Zilber's quasiminimal excellent classes, not atomic classes of a complete first-order theory. The result is that one axiom of that setting is redundant.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record); five named authors
checked_by.what_they_did: Published. I saw the abstract and bibliographic record.

events.direction: Neighbouring result. Does not bear on the direction of the bullet.

events.what_happened: M. C. Laskowski and S. Shelah, 'A strong failure of aleph_0-stability for atomic classes', arXiv 1701.05474 (submitted 19 Jan 2017), Arch. Math. Logic 58 (2019) 99-118. For the class At_T of atomic models of a countable complete first-order T: if At_T is not pcl-small (some atomic model realises uncountably many types over pcl(a) for some finite tuple a), then T has 2^{aleph_1} pairwise non-isomorphic atomic models, each of size aleph_1. The abstract does not mention categoricity.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only. Journal version (2019) not opened.
events.delivers: A dichotomy at aleph_1 for atomic models of a countable complete T: failure of pcl-smallness gives 2^{aleph_1} atomic models of size aleph_1. By contraposition, an atomic class with exactly one model of size aleph_1 must be pcl-small. This is my inference from the abstract, not a claim the paper makes. The paper establishes no categoricity in any cardinal.
events.remains: The whole bullet. The paper is about aleph_0-stability failure and counts of aleph_1 models.

checked_by.who: Archive for Mathematical Logic (refereed journal of record); authors M. C. Laskowski and S. Shelah
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2019. I read the arXiv abstract only.

events.direction: Neither way on the bullet. A structural dichotomy for aleph_1 atomic models.

events.what_happened: J. T. Baldwin, M. C. Laskowski and S. Shelah, 'When does aleph_1-categoricity imply omega-stability?', arXiv 2308.13942 (v1 submitted 26 Aug 2023); Model Theory 3(3) (2024) 801-823, DOI 10.2140/mt.2024.3.801. Main theorem per the abstract: if an atomic class At is aleph_1-categorical and has a model of size (2^{aleph_0})^+ (written beth_1^+ in the abstract), then At is omega-stable. The paper also clarifies the space of types over the unique model of size aleph_1. Its Section 1 restates Shelah's ZFC excellence results and the very-weak-GCH converse, and asks: does an aleph_1-categorical atomic class have arbitrarily large models? It notes Shelah showed such a class has a model in aleph_2. A Shelah talk recorded 17 Jan 2023 (CIRM; published 13 Feb 2023) announced the aleph_1 step as work in preparation: categoricity in aleph_1 with a model of cardinality above 2^{aleph_0} gives aleph_0-stability, described as 'the first case of excellence'. Per the protocol, that talk is dated here to the write-up, not to the talk.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only, per the abstract page. Search reported a PDF copy dated 7 Apr 2024 at NSF PAR, not opened. The journal version is Model Theory 3(3) (2024). Shelah's archive lists this as paper 1244 and says the website copy may be newer; not checked.
events.delivers: The aleph_1 case only, under a size hypothesis: for atomic classes, aleph_1-categoricity together with a model of size (2^{aleph_0})^+ implies omega-stability. It does not establish categoricity in any cardinal other than aleph_1, does not establish excellence, and does not establish arbitrarily large models.
events.remains: Whether an aleph_1-categorical atomic class has models of arbitrarily large size, which the paper poses as open. Without it, the Shelah ZFC transfer to all uncountable cardinals is not reached. The paper does not treat aleph_n for n >= 2, or aleph_0 and the finite cardinals.

checked_by.who: Model Theory (MSP journal, refereed); the three paper authors
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2024, vol. 3 no. 3. I did not open the journal page; the journal reference is from the arXiv abstract page.

events.direction: Partial positive in the aleph_1 case: aleph_1-categoricity plus a model of size (2^{aleph_0})^+ forces omega-stability, the atomic-class analogue of the first-order step in Morley's proof. It cuts toward the bullet's conclusion only indirectly, through omega-stability. It does not supply categoricity in other cardinals.

events.what_happened: J. T. Baldwin, M. C. Laskowski and S. Shelah, 'An analogue of U-rank for atomic classes', arXiv 2502.00984 (submitted 3 Feb 2025, one version). For the atomic class At_T of a countable complete first-order T they develop a U-rank analogue. Per the abstract and the html text I read: if some type tp(d/a) is not ranked, there are 2^{aleph_1} non-isomorphic atomic models of size aleph_1. If all types have finite rank, the rank is fully additive and every finite tuple is dominated by an independent set of realisations of pseudo-minimal types. Thm 5.4.2 as quoted by the fetch: 'If AtT has <2^aleph1 non-isomorphic atomic models of size aleph1, then AtT is ranked.'
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet's categoricity question in the parts I read. The results are about ranks and the number of aleph_1 atomic models. The introduction mentions categoricity only as background (Morley's theorem, Shelah's aleph_omega result, the aleph_1 goal). The fetch covered the first 100,000 characters only, to about Section 5.3.
events.direction: Neighbouring result. On what I read it does not change the bullet's status.

events.what_happened: J. T. Baldwin and C. C. Brincus, 'Categoricity for an inferential omega-logic and in L_{omega1,omega}', arXiv 2602.02854 (v1 2 Feb 2026; v2 25 Apr 2026, current). The abstract says the paper gives two extensions of first-order logic by omega-rules and characterises the countable structures whose theory in each logic is categorical, meaning has a unique model. The abstract does not mention atomic classes or any cardinal other than countable.
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet. A different logic (omega-rule extensions of first-order logic) and a different notion of categoricity (a unique model of the theory).
events.direction: Neighbouring. Not on the direction of the bullet.

events.what_happened: J. T. Baldwin and J. Nagloo, 'Categoricity and non-arithmetic Fuchsian groups', arXiv 2602.11432 (submitted 11 Feb 2026, one version). Introduces an L_{omega1,omega} axiomatisation T^infty_SF of the covering map j_Gamma for a non-arithmetic Fuchsian group of the first kind with finite covolume. Shows it is categorical in all infinite cardinalities, extending Daw and Harris in the arithmetic case. Shows the first-order theory of j_Gamma is complete, admits quantifier elimination, and is omega-stable.
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet. It is an L_{omega1,omega} axiomatisation of one specific covering map, categorical in all infinite cardinalities. It is not an atomic class and says nothing about the aleph_n hypothesis.
events.direction: Neighbouring. The conclusion 'categorical in all infinite cardinalities' is for a different sentence.
events.object: The L_{omega1,omega} sentence T^infty_SF, axiomatising the covering map j_Gamma for a non-arithmetic Fuchsian group. The abstract reports it is categorical in all infinite cardinalities. The explicit axioms were not read.

events.what_happened: J. L. Goh and C.-M. Tran, 'Categoricity without Power', arXiv 2605.00697 (submitted 1 May 2026, one version). Per the abstract as fetched: 'We prove an analogue of Morley's categoricity theorem where cardinality is replaced by the recursion-theoretic notion', with D-categoricity for complete arithmetically definable theories. The paper states that under ZFC, D-categoricity for some nonzero arithmetic degree is equivalent to uncountable categoricity.
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet. It is an analogue of Morley's theorem with arithmetic degrees in place of cardinality, for arithmetically definable theories. It is not about atomic classes or aleph_n.
events.direction: Neighbouring. An analogue of Morley's theorem with a different notion of 'size'.

events.what_happened: J. Freitag and S. Mutchnik, 'A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture', arXiv 2609.00436 (submitted 31 Aug 2026, one version, 21 pages). Abstract: 'Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture. This answers a long-standing open question of Hart, Kim and Pillay (1996).' Section 1.1 of the preprint: 'This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.' The counterexample is described by secondary sources as the theory of an infinite-dimensional vector space over the division ring of fractions of the quantum graph algebra of the random graph. I did not confirm this object in the text I read.
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet. It concerns the stable forking conjecture for simple theories (Hart, Kim and Pillay, 1996), not atomic classes or categoricity at aleph_n. Recorded because it is an AI-credited model-theory result in the window.
events.directly_checkable: The counterexample is a specific structure per secondary sources. I did not check it.
events.doubts: Non-peer-reviewed preprint. A Breakthrough Tracker record calls the negative resolution provisional and says no independent specialist assessment, formal proof or separate construction was located (record last checked 4 Sept 2026). That is a tracker, not a specialist report, and I found no specialist response in my searches.
events.direction: Negative for the stable forking conjecture as stated by Hart, Kim and Pillay: forking in a simple theory is claimed not always to be witnessed by a stable formula. This is not a direction on the bullet.
events.object: Per secondary sources, the theory of an infinite-dimensional vector space over the division ring of fractions of the quantum graph algebra of the random graph. The abstract says only that it is a counterexample. Whether this is the object in the paper was not verified.

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors' section 1.1: 'we prompted ChatGPT to construct a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture with a detailed series of prompts'. The abstract calls it 'ChatGPT 5.6'. Also in the paper: 'AI was used for proofreading, with the edits performed and evaluated manually by the authors.' The authors also write that 'The proofs of the relevant facts around the counterexample as well as some aspects of the specific setup have been written entirely by the authors, and no AI tool was used in the actual writing of this manuscript.' Their title-block footnote says the arguments 'were based on proofs generated using JF's ChatGPT account'.
systems.basis_quote: This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.

ai.disclosed_cost: Title-block footnote: one author 'received a grant of access to ChatGPT Pro through OpenAI's academic researcher support program'. No compute, token or monetary figure is given.

events.what_happened: T. Kihara, 'Atomic toposes, choice spectra and model-theoretic stability', arXiv 2609.21111 (submitted 17 Sep 2026, one version; math.LO, cross-listed math.CT). Studies atomic sheaf toposes over categories of structures of bounded cardinality, relating Galois lambda-stability to choice principles for those toposes. 'Atomic' is in the topos-theoretic sense, not the sense of atomic models of a first-order theory. A search-index excerpt reports an acknowledgement saying ChatGPT (named GPT-5.6 Sol) was used extensively in exploratory proof development and Claude Opus 5 in local peer review. I could not open that acknowledgement; see ai.
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet. It is a Galois-stability and choice result for atomic sheaf toposes, not the categoricity of atomic models of a first-order theory at aleph_n.
events.doubts: The acknowledgement that the search index attributes to this paper could not be confirmed. The text I could open (abstract page and html to about section 8.4) contains no AI mention, and the tail of the html was not reached.
events.direction: Neighbouring. Not on the bullet's direction.

disputes.summary: The Freitag-Mutchnik preprint gives two accounts of who wrote the proofs. The title-block footnote says the arguments are 'based on proofs generated using JF's ChatGPT account'. Section 1.1 says the proofs of the relevant facts 'have been written entirely by the authors'. Both are recorded as the authors' words and are not reconciled here. This concerns a different problem from the bullet.

summary: The bullet is confirmed verbatim in the Model theory and formal languages section of the frozen Wikipedia list (fetched; the neighbouring bullets are not about categoricity). Its status rests on pre-window work. Shelah's ZFC theorem (1983) says that if an atomic class is excellent and has an uncountable model, categoricity in one uncountable cardinal gives categoricity in all uncountable cardinals. Excellence is a hypothesis there. The converse, that categoricity in every aleph_n gives excellence, holds only under the very weak GCH (2^{aleph_n} < 2^{aleph_{n+1}} for all n), as the 2023 paper cites it. Lessmann (2003) gives the same transfer for excellent classes with a pregeometry argument. The single-aleph_1 step is Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah (arXiv 26 Aug 2023; Model Theory 2024). It shows that aleph_1-categoricity plus a model of size (2^{aleph_0})^+ forces omega-stability, and it poses the open question whether an aleph_1-categorical atomic class has arbitrarily large models (Shelah showed a model in aleph_2). A Shelah talk recorded in January 2023 announced the aleph_1 result as work in preparation, and I have dated it to the 2023 write-up. Nothing I found after 26 January 2024 settles or moves the question. The in-window atomic-class paper (Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah, U-rank, 3 Feb 2025) does not address categoricity on what I read. Baldwin's 25 Feb 2025 seminar abstract still lists the L_{omega1,omega} analogues as open. The in-window AI-credited model-theory preprint (Freitag-Mutchnik, stable forking, 31 Aug 2026, which names GPT-5.6 Sol in its section 1.1) concerns a different problem. Kihara's atomic-toposes preprint is off-topic; a search excerpt reports an AI acknowledgement that I could not confirm in the text I could open. I found no AI involvement in any event that bears on this bullet. Two readings of the bullet matter. Read as a single aleph_n, it is open as far as the sources show. Read as every aleph_n, Shelah's 1983 result with the very weak GCH answers it for uncountable cardinals, conditionally and before the window. Neither reading covers aleph_0 or the finite cardinals, and the Wikipedia wording does not say T is countable, though every source assumes it. Other leads I could not turn into events are listed under incomplete.
competing_reading: Read with the every-aleph_n hypothesis, and with the very weak GCH accepted, the bullet is answered for uncountable cardinals by Shelah's 1983 theorem, with no in-window work needed. A reader who takes the aleph_1 talk and the 2024 paper together could also treat the single-aleph_1 case as nearly settled, since they give ZFC excellence-type behaviour once a model of size (2^{aleph_0})^+ exists. Against that, the size hypothesis is not known to hold for every aleph_1-categorical atomic class, so the single-n case stays open. The aleph_0 and finite cardinals are not covered by any source.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Shelah 1983 Parts A and B: whether excellence follows from categoricity in one aleph_n, or whether the very weak GCH converse is needed. (2) A ZFC proof or refutation that an aleph_1-categorical atomic class is excellent, or has arbitrarily large models (the question Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah pose). (3) The write-up of the Shelah aleph_1 result announced in January 2023 as work in preparation. (4) The Baldwin Categoricity book (2009), Appendix D 'Problems', which is probably where the bullet's wording comes from. It would fix whether 'the aleph_n' means one n or every n, and whether T is countable. (5) The 2024 Baylor talk PDF (see incomplete).
